question.text: Sunlight of intensity <math><mn>1.3</mn><mi> </mi><mi>k</mi><mi>W</mi><mi> </mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> is incident normally on a thin convex lens of focal length <math><mn>20</mn><mi> </mi><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math> . Ignore the energy loss of light due to the lens and assume that the lens aperture size is much smaller than its focal length. The average intensity of light, in <math><mi>k</mi><mi>W</mi><mi> </mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> , at a distance <math><mn>22</mn><mi> </mi><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math> from the lens on the other side is __________.

solution.text:
rR=220=110
∴   Ratio of area =1100
Let energy incident on lens be E
∴   Given EA=1.3
E=A×1.30
Also aA=1100
∴   Average intensity of light at 22 cm=Ea=A×1.3a=100×1.3=130k W/m2
